title: review follow-ups of PR #35671: fleet-roster's closingRefs is an unregistered fourth closing-keyword parser
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgU8spV5rNhbE4uG8Va

Filing gate: ① a named defect with a reproduction, filed as the L1/L2 follow-ups card of PR #35671 (an out-of-scope finding its dev reported, same lane, outside that diff) · Source: fleet

## What is wrong

`scripts/pm/fleet-roster.mjs` `closingRefs` (on `origin/main`, unchanged by PR #35671) reads a pull's closing keywords with its own regex, `\b(?:fix(?:e[sd])?|close[sd]?|resolve[sd]?)\s*:?\s+(?:OWNER/NAME)?#(\d+)\b`. `scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` registers three parsers of that grammar (`PARSERS`) and two known non-parsers (`NON_PARSERS`), and its header item 5 says: "THE SWEEP. No FOURTH parser of this grammar exists unregistered." `closingRefs` is that fourth parser, and the sweep does not see it: `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` exits 0 and `--list` shows 3 parsers and 2 non-parsers, because neither `SIGNATURES` shape matches this spelling.

The two readings differ (measured by PR #35671's dev against the shared parser):
- `Fixes:#N` and `Fixes#N` bind in the shared parser and do NOT bind in `closingRefs`.
- A backticked `` `Fixes #N` `` and `Fixes` followed by a newline and `#N` bind in `closingRefs` and do NOT bind in the shared parser.

## Why it matters

`closingRefs` feeds the roster's awaiting-landing and awaiting-merge columns and the in-flight attribution of pulls (`fleet-roster.mjs` lines 453, 460 and 635 on `origin/main`). A pull whose body writes `Fixes:#N` is missing from its card's row; a pull whose body only quotes a keyword in backticks (an L1 note, a "do not write `Fixes #N`" line) is counted as closing a card it does not close. The maintainer reads the roster for which seat has what waiting, so the row is wrong in exactly the two cases above; and the parity gate, whose job is to stop a fourth grammar, reports clean.

## Suggested fix (the dispatching seat measures)

1. `closingRefs` reads through the one shared closing-keyword parser (the one `check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` registers), so the roster binds what GitHub binds; its three self-test cases move with it and gain the two divergent spellings.
2. The parity sweep's `SIGNATURES` learns the optional-colon spelling, so a fifth copy of this regex is caught; a planted specimen in its self-test proves it.

Reader: the seat that next edits `scripts/pm/fleet-roster.mjs` (area:fleet, seat repo:objectstack#1); as a p3 it rides a p1/p2 PR on the same file.

Grading: area:fleet · Task · Impeded (the roster misreads two body spellings; the cards themselves close correctly) · fleet tooling, rare · evidence: read from the code on `origin/main` and the dev's measurement on PR #35671.
Suggested grade: p3 (a tooling Task, default p3; no decision or landing of the fleet goes wrong beyond the roster's display).

Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue closingRefs` → 1 hit (#35237, the parent card of PR #35671, not this finding); `fleet-roster closing keyword` → 23 hits, none on this parser; `fourth parser closing` → 99 hits, the nearest (#17533, #18435, both closed) are about other parity gaps.
